title: Amazoff Is Expanding Same-Day Delivery to Three More Cities
author: editor@example.com
summary: Same-day delivery now covers Plovdiv, Varna, and Burgas, alongside our existing Sofia coverage.
content:
Same-day delivery, previously available only within Sofia, is now live in Plovdiv, Varna, and Burgas for orders placed before 2pm local time.

This has been the single most requested feature from customers outside the capital since we launched the service, and it's rolling out gradually rather than all at once - courier capacity in each city needs to build up to reliably support the volume before we widen the postcode coverage further.

For now, coverage in each new city is limited to central postcodes, with wider coverage expanding over the coming months as courier partnerships scale. The order page will clearly show whether same-day delivery is available for your address at checkout - if it isn't shown as an option, standard 2-4 day delivery still applies as before.

Cash on delivery remains available alongside same-day delivery in all four cities, so this isn't limited to card payments only.

We'll continue expanding city by city as courier capacity allows, and this page will be updated as new cities go live.
seo_title: Same-Day Delivery Now in Plovdiv, Varna, and Burgas | Amazoff
seo_description: Amazoff's same-day delivery service has expanded beyond Sofia to Plovdiv, Varna, and Burgas.

title: A Note on Our Return Policy Update
author: editor@example.com
summary: We've extended our standard return window from 14 to 30 days. Here's what changed and why.
content:
Starting this month, our standard return window has been extended from 14 to 30 days for most product categories, giving customers more time to decide whether an item is right for them.

The change came directly from customer feedback - 14 days was consistently cited as too tight, particularly for larger purchases like furniture or electronics that people want to properly live with before deciding to keep them. A longer window also reduces the pressure to make a rushed return decision.

A few categories remain on shorter or different terms for practical reasons: underwear and swimwear for hygiene reasons, and made-to-order or personalised items, which cannot be resold once customised. These exceptions are clearly marked on the relevant product pages.

The return process itself hasn't changed - items still need to be in their original, unused condition with tags or packaging intact where applicable. Refunds are processed to the original payment method once the returned item is received and checked.

This applies to all orders placed from today onward. Orders placed before this update remain under the previous 14-day window, as stated in the terms at the time of purchase.
seo_title: Updated Return Policy - 30 Day Returns | Amazoff
seo_description: Amazoff has extended its standard return window from 14 to 30 days across most product categories.

title: Introducing Cash on Delivery for All Bulgarian Postcodes
author: editor@example.com
summary: Cash on delivery, previously limited to major cities, is now available nationwide.
content:
Cash on delivery is now available for every postcode we ship to in Bulgaria, removing the previous limitation to major cities only.

This has been a gradual rollout tied to courier network coverage - COD requires the courier to actually collect payment on delivery, which meant it could only launch in areas where our courier partners had the operational setup to handle cash handling reliably. That coverage has now caught up to our full delivery footprint.

At checkout, cash on delivery will now appear as a payment option for any address within our delivery zone, alongside our existing card payment option. A small COD handling fee applies, shown clearly at checkout before you confirm the order - this covers the additional handling cost on the courier side rather than being a hidden charge.

Card payment remains available everywhere as before, and both payment methods carry the same delivery timeframes and return policy - COD isn't a second-class option, just an alternative for anyone who prefers to pay on arrival.
seo_title: Cash on Delivery Now Available Nationwide | Amazoff
seo_description: Cash on delivery is now available for every postcode Amazoff delivers to across Bulgaria.

title: How We Pick Which Brands Make It Onto Amazoff
author: editor@example.com
summary: A look at what our buying team actually checks before a new brand gets listed.
content:
We get asked fairly often how a brand ends up on Amazoff, and the honest answer is that it's a more deliberate process than it might look from the outside - not every brand that applies gets listed, and the reasons are usually practical rather than arbitrary.

The first filter is basic product safety and compliance documentation. Any brand selling in a regulated category - electronics, anything with a plug, children's items - needs to provide certification before we'll even consider the listing, regardless of how good the product looks. This isn't negotiable and it's the single most common reason an application doesn't proceed.

Beyond compliance, our buying team looks at return rate data from similar products already in the category, build quality reports from independent testing where available, and - increasingly - how a brand handles its own customer service, since a brand's return and warranty process becomes our problem too once we're selling their products.

We also deliberately avoid listing multiple near-identical products from different brands purely to pad category count. If a new brand's product doesn't meaningfully differ from something we already carry - on price, quality, or feature set - it's a harder sell internally, even if the brand itself is reputable.

None of this means every product we list is perfect - reviews exist for a reason, and we read them. But the baseline bar for getting listed at all is higher than a lot of customers probably assume.
seo_title: How Amazoff Selects Brands to List | Amazoff
seo_description: A behind-the-scenes look at how our buying team decides which brands and products make it onto Amazoff.

title: A Look Inside Our Warehouse Ahead of the Holiday Season
author: editor@example.com
summary: How we're preparing for the busiest weeks of the year, and what it means for delivery times.
content:
The weeks around the holiday season are consistently our busiest of the year, and preparation for it starts months in advance rather than being something we scramble to handle as volume picks up.

On the warehouse side, this means temporary staff onboarding starting in early autumn, additional shelving capacity brought online for the highest-demand categories, and stress-testing our picking and packing workflow against volumes well above what a normal week looks like, so the system doesn't buckle under the real thing.

For customers, the practical impact is mostly around setting expectations early. Delivery estimates during peak weeks are naturally a little longer than our normal 2-4 day standard, and we'll flag this clearly at checkout during the busiest period rather than letting an optimistic estimate slip. Ordering earlier in the season, where possible, remains the most reliable way to guarantee arrival before a specific date.

Stock planning is the other major piece - our most popular gift categories are ordered in significantly larger volumes ahead of the season based on prior years' data, though a genuinely unexpected trending product can still sell through faster than restocking allows, which is simply a reality of retail at this scale.

We'll keep communicating clearly about cutoff dates for guaranteed holiday delivery as the season approaches.
seo_title: Preparing for the Holiday Season | Amazoff
seo_description: A look at how Amazoff prepares its warehouse and delivery operations for the busiest weeks of the year.

title: Gift Guide: Ten Things Under 50 Leva
author: editor@example.com
summary: Thoughtful gift ideas across categories that won't stretch the budget - updated for this season.
content:
Finding a genuinely good gift under 50 leva usually means avoiding the obvious "cheap gift" aisle and looking instead at smaller, well-made items from categories people don't expect a gift from.

From kitchen, a well-made utensil set or a good coffee scoop-and-canister pair reads as more thoughtful than it costs, especially for anyone who cooks regularly and appreciates tools that actually work well rather than just look nice.

From beauty, a quality lipstick or a small skincare set in a shade or formula suited to the recipient shows more consideration than a generic gift basket, provided you have some sense of what they already use.

From accessories, a silk scarf or a well-made crossbody bag both sit comfortably in this budget and work across a wide range of personal styles, making them a safer choice than clothing sized to fit.

For anyone active, quality socks or a well-cushioned pair of athletic crew socks sound like an underwhelming gift on paper but are consistently well received - everyone needs them, nobody buys the good ones for themselves, and they fit under any budget with room to spare.

The common thread across all of these: pick something the person wouldn't quite buy for themselves, in a category they already care about. That does more work than price ever will.
seo_title: Gift Guide: Ten Ideas Under 50 Leva | Amazoff
seo_description: Thoughtful gift ideas under 50 leva across kitchen, beauty, accessories, and sportswear categories.

title: Draft: New Loyalty Programme Notes (Internal Review)
author: editor@example.com
summary: Early draft covering the proposed points-based loyalty programme structure - not yet finalised.
content:
This is an early working draft outlining a proposed points-based loyalty programme, kept here for internal review before anything is finalised or announced publicly.

The rough structure under discussion: customers earn points per leva spent, redeemable against future orders at a fixed conversion rate. Additional points would be awarded for actions beyond direct spending - leaving a verified review, referring a new customer whose first order completes successfully, and reaching account milestones like a first anniversary as a registered customer.

Open questions still being worked through include whether points should expire after a period of inactivity, how returned orders affect already-earned points on that purchase, and whether COD orders should earn points differently from card orders given the different risk profile at time of order versus at time of delivery.

Nothing here is confirmed and none of these numbers or mechanics should be treated as final. This draft exists purely to consolidate discussion points before the programme design is locked down and communicated properly.
